newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists want poor countries in EMU.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists want poor countries in EMU.

text.p: France's opposition Socialist party, preparing its manifesto for parliamentary elections in 1998, called for European monetary union to include poorer countries from its launch in 1999.

In a draft economic and social programme to be presented to a conference of party militants on Saturday, the Socialists, in opposition since 1993, reaffirmed support for the launch of the single European currency, the euro.
But they set several conditions, including that the single currency area must not be limited to a hard core of rich states that would exclude Italy and Spain.

The draft also backs a European programme to encourage economic growth, the establishment of a "real European government" able to set economic and exchange rate policy and a revision of the exchange rate between the dollar and the euro.
Socialist leader Lionel Jospin has said previously that the euro should be at parity with the dollar -- implying a big devaluation in the euro against the U.S. currency.

The draft programme, still subject to amendments, also calls for a national conference on wages to discuss ways of encouraging growth by raising purchasing power and for cuts in working hours to boost employment.
The programme is due to be adopted by a national party conference on December 14 and 15.
